title: Geopolitical Daily
email_subject: Iran celebrates as US troops leave Iraq
preheader: The pullout closes a deployment begun in 2014 and leaves a gap Iran and ISIS may fill.
intro_text: Good morning. It's Wednesday, September 30, 2026 — the 3 stories that matter most today, plus 8 quick updates from around the world.

stories.story_title: US forces exit Iraq after two decades
stories.why_important: The last US forces left their remaining bases in Iraq on Wednesday. This ends a deployment that began in 2014 to fight the Islamic State. The pullout is mostly popular among Iraqis, but it raises fear of a security gap. Iran's allies and ISIS can exploit that gap.
stories.what_overlooked: President Biden's administration agreed to the timetable in 2024, and President Trump's administration carried it out. Supporters on both sides skip the fact it continued, and Tehran called the exit a victory.
stories.prediction: Whether Iraqi forces take over the vacated bases or Iran-backed militias move in first will show who controls the west.

stories.story_title: Supreme Court lets Trump resume deportations to third countries
stories.why_important: A 6-3 Supreme Court order lets the administration keep sending migrants to countries where they have no ties. It does not first let them object, and the court hears arguments in December. So the policy can run for months before the justices rule.
stories.what_overlooked: A federal appeals court is separately weighing whether the administration defied a judge. That judge ordered planes carrying Venezuelans to El Salvador to turn around in March 2025.
stories.prediction: Whether immigration authorities send new notices this week to remove migrants to a third country will show how fast they use the order.

stories.story_title: French strikes and school protests challenge Macron's budget cuts
stories.why_important: Government workers struck nationwide, and high school students blocked schools, while police arrested 440 students. The unrest over planned budget cuts is growing ahead of next year's presidential election, weakening Macron at home.
stories.what_overlooked: Protests began in the Paris region, where about 10 schools were blockaded on Tuesday. They then spread to other cities, a sign the movement is not led from Paris.
stories.prediction: Whether unions call a second nationwide strike day this week will show if the movement holds after Tuesday's arrests.

quick_hits.text: A Flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv landed in Saudi Arabia after its two pilots fought, and Israel briefly scrambled warplanes.
Spain's cabinet agreed to ban evictions until 2030 after the forced removal of an 87-year-old Madrid woman sparked nationwide protests.
Morocco's king appointed Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri as the country's first woman prime minister after her party won September elections.
Russian strikes on Kyiv and the surrounding region killed three people, including a child, and wounded seven.
Trump and six tech CEOs signed a voluntary accord on AI safety audits and oversight while rejecting new government rules.
South Africa's president ordered action on femicide after 11 women's bodies were found east of Johannesburg since July.
India's foreign minister said Washington's failure to grasp India's terrorism concerns about Pakistan is straining ties.
A Nigerian court dealt Dangote's Lagos refinery a setback as the tycoon demanded a 'level playing field' against fuel importers.

views.framing: US withdrawal risks a security vacuum that Iran-backed militias and Islamic State could exploit.
views.quote: Iraqi officials and analysts warn the departure could embolden Iran-backed militias and give Islamic State group fighters room to rebuild their capabilities.

views.framing: US exit opens Iraq to Iranian influence, while some Iraqis see the withdrawal as premature.
views.quote: While the eventual departure of U.S. forces is broadly popular among Iraqis, those who worry about the strength of the Iran-backed groups fear the withdrawal is premature
